text: A pharmaceutical industry plant is conducting an annual assessment to its carbon footprint using the GHG Protocol. text: Answer the following questions based on the following: Ranking is an instrument to reward the best performers — but more importantly it signals the best way to do things. EIA started way back in 1994 when development projects were few and the process remained uncontested. The rot took hold from the early 2000s when “building” projects were included in this system of scrutiny. There is no question that construction especially large-scale housing, infrastructure, or commercial projects, has a massive environmental footprint. They add to water usage, wastewater generation traffic, and to solid. waste. The problem was the system was never upgraded to handle the huge volume of “building” projects. This led to delays and high i transaction costs — corruption, in other words. So in 2006, MoEFCC decentralized and outsourced the work to states. text: Case 38 hotels in Mahabaleshwar-Panchgani to close In what must be the most punitive action taken so far the Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) on Friday ordered the closure of the 38 leading hotels in eco-sensitive hill-station of Mahabaleshwar-Panchgani for polluting Venna lake and the Koyna valley with untreated sewage. The hotels are charged with violation of the Water (Prevention & Control of Pollution) Act,1974. MPCB member secretary said “the untreated sewage had left a toxic trail, forcing Board to take action. We have asked local administration to disconnect electricity and water supply to these hotels with immediate effect.” MPCB had asked these hotels to upgrade their treatment facilities to comply with environmental protection rules,1986 & to provide common waste processing facilities for solid waste management within three months. After giving enough time these hotels never bothered to comply with. MPCB’s stringent action comes as action in response to PIL and continuous fight by Bombay Environment Action Group (BEAG) to protect these hill stations from deforestation and environmental degradation . BEAG has also filed PIL against dumping garbage and sewage water in lake by these hotels for decades. This is major drinking water source for the region. Court has directed Mahabaleshwar- Panchgani Municipality to give court regular progress on the ruling. It has directed the state to demarcate forest areas of Mahabaleshwar-Panchgani hill station.

text: Case: Mushroom Composters In 1978, Mushroom Composters Pvt. Limited set up mushroom composting operations in Ebenezer, a town at the outskirts of Sydney, Australia. The facility composted poultry manure, straw and other ingredients by letting them rot. PTO ~ va In 1992, residents of the area found that a very foul odour was being emitted from the factory. The odour was so foul that most residents had to keep the windows shut at all times. This was the case even in summer, leading to considerable difficulty for the residents. In addition to this, children at the local school also started taking ill due to the odours. The residents under the Ebenezer Concerned Residents Committee decided to move to court protesting against the facility operations under the appropriate legislation. Since the committee was an unincorporated body and under Australian Law an unincorporated body cannot bring enforcement proceedings, a gentleman by the name of Peter Foster filed a law suit against the erring company. During the course of the case it was established through witnesses that the odours did exist and were degrading the quality of the air in the region. It was also established through expert witnesses that such odours would arise from bacterial activity in composting under anaerobic conditions. This was found to be breach of the consent given to the company to set up the plant. Under the consent, the company was to conduct its composing activity under strictly aerobic conditions. The judge in the case found the company guilty of polluting the environment and ordered the immediate shifting of the facility. This order was suspended for 12 months, in order to allow the company some time to shift the facility. However the tale didn’t end here.

subject: Environment Management
text: year later, the company was still polluting in the same area in the contempt of the court orders. In fact during the period the company had even earned a profit of $230,000 while operating in contempt! Peter Foster immediately brought proceedings for contempt of court. Foster led evidence from 35 local residents that the odours continued. Additional evidence came to the surface that the company was aware of technology that would reduce the odours since 1991, but did not implement the same as it was too expensive. The Court found that the company” ....took decisions largely for commercial reasons, which involved a willful or deliberate breach of(the Court’s) order”. In a landmark ruling, the court ordered the firm to pay a fine of $80,000 with further penalties amounting to $8,000 for each week it continued to remain in contempt. While not as much as the profit made by the company, this was by far one of the largest fine imposed by the Court then. Although this is a case of Australian origin, the situation in India could be similar.
